sections.h2: Where is the Wayne County Register of Deeds and when is it open?
sections.html:
The office is at 224-226 E Walnut Street, Suite 100, in Goldsboro, and the phone is 919-731-1449. The county's Register of Deeds page lists general hours of 8:00 to 5:00, with real estate filings accepted from 8:00 to 4:45 without an appointment.

The office asks that instruments for recording not be brought in after 4:45 p.m. If a closing is running late, send documents electronically instead, or plan to record the next business day.

  • Real estate filings: 8:00 to 4:45
  • Notary oaths and vital records: 8:15 to 4:45
  • Marriage licenses: 8:00 to 4:00

sections.h2: What does the Wayne County Register of Deeds record?
sections.html:
It records, indexes and stores deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions and cancellations, powers of attorney, assumed business names, separation agreements and similar filings. Records go back to 1913, and most real estate records can be searched online from 1971 forward.

The office is a recording office only. State law bars its staff from practicing law, so they cannot draft a deed, explain what a document does or supply legal forms. A seller who needs a deed prepared should use an attorney, and many closings run through a title company or closing lawyer who handles recording.

Wills are not filed here. The county directs people to the Clerk of Courts at 919-722-6100 for wills.

sections.h2: Can I record a Wayne County deed electronically?
sections.html:
Yes. The office accepts all document types by eRecording, and the eRecording page says plats can now be recorded electronically as well. Banks, law firms and title companies must first pick one of the office's authorized providers.

The provider walks the firm through a submitter agreement. Once the provider processes it, the Register of Deeds emails a unique identification number within two business days, and that number is needed for every electronic filing.

Individual sellers do not sign up. Your closing attorney or title company usually holds the account. The county page notes that providers must be approved under G.S. 47-14(a1).

sections.h2: What does recording cost in Wayne County?
sections.html:
Statewide recording fees in effect in Wayne County under G.S. 161-10
ItemFee as printed
Instrument in general$26.00 for the first 15 pages, $4.00 each additional page
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 for the first 35 pages, $4.00 each additional page
Satisfaction or cancellationNo fee
Plat$21.00 per sheet
Certified copy$5.00 first page, $2.00 each additional
Nonstandard document$25.00 extra

The statute calls these fees complete and exclusive, collected before filing (G.S. 161-10). Call the Wayne office to confirm the current schedule before you pay.

sections.h2: Who pays the excise tax on a Wayne County deed?
sections.html:
The seller, called the transferor, pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. The rate is one dollar for each five hundred dollars, or fractional part, of the price or value conveyed (G.S. 105-228.30).

The county keeps half and sends the other half to the Department of Revenue each month. If a parcel spans more than one county, the tax goes to the county holding the greater value.

Your settlement statement shows the amount. Check it against the sale price on the deed.

sections.h2: Which other Wayne County filings come up around a home sale?
sections.html:
Several documents beyond the deed can touch a sale. A power of attorney, if someone signs for the owner, is recorded with the office. An assumed business name for a rental operation is also filed there, and so are separation agreements that affect who holds title.

Veterans can also have a discharge, the DD-214, recorded with the office, which is useful when you later apply for the disabled veteran property tax exclusion.

Seller financing creates its own recording duty. Under Chapter 47H, a contract for deed on a one to four family home or manufactured home must be recorded, or a memorandum of it, within five business days, and the buyer can cancel until midnight of the third business day (Chapter 47H).

sections.h2: What do Wayne County housing figures say about recording activity?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's Wayne County QuickFacts lists 47,507 households, with 86.1% of residents living in the same house a year earlier. Most owners stay put, so a given deed history tends to be long.

  • Median monthly owner cost with a mortgage: $1,367
  • Median monthly owner cost without one: $451
  • Median gross rent: $965
  • Veterans, 2020-2024: 9,996

A long ownership means older deeds of trust that may never have been formally released. If you inherited or bought a long held Wayne County house, look for a paid off loan with no recorded satisfaction, since the lender can fix that at no filing cost.

Foreclosure sales and tax foreclosure sales also end up in these records. Under state law the sale of a foreclosed home is followed by upset bid periods of ten days, so the title is not final the day of the auction (G.S. 45-21.27).

sections.h2: Why does recording order matter on a Wayne County sale?
sections.html:
A deed or deed of trust does not bind lien creditors or later buyers who paid value until it is registered in the county where the land lies. Priority follows the order and time of registration (G.S. 47-18).

That is why a closing lawyer records quickly after funding. For a sale where an old lien or unreleased deed of trust sits on the title, search the Wayne records first, and ask the lender for a satisfaction that is then recorded, which costs nothing to file.

  • Search the grantor index for open deeds of trust
  • Confirm satisfactions were recorded
  • Pay the excise tax with the deed
  • Record the new deed and any new loan

The register of deeds is an elected county officer, according to G.S. 161-1.

sections.h2: What steps should a Wayne County seller take before the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
Work through the checklist with your closing attorney, because the register of deeds only records what is presented and cannot review its legal effect.

  • Check that the legal description on the deed matches your vesting deed.
  • Find old deeds of trust and ask each lender for a recorded satisfaction.
  • Get a payoff from the Wayne County Tax Collector for the year's bill.
  • Bring the excise tax payment, based on the price or value conveyed.
  • Confirm the notary acknowledgment is complete before you hand it over.

If you cannot attend closing, a recorded power of attorney may let someone sign for you. The register of deeds records those as well, so ask the closing office whether the lender and the title insurer will accept it.

Foreclosed owners have extra steps. Tenants under leases signed or renewed on or after October 1, 2007 may end a lease on at least 10 and no more than 90 days' notice after a foreclosure sale date, according to G.S. 45-21.16A.

faqs.q: Does the Wayne County Register of Deeds prepare deeds?
faqs.a: No. The office only records documents and cannot give legal advice, supply legal forms or help complete them. Use an attorney or a closing office for drafting.

faqs.q: How far back do Wayne County records go?
faqs.a: The office's records go back to 1913, and most real estate records are searchable online from 1971 onward. Older land records may need an in-person search.

faqs.q: Can a title company eRecord in Wayne County?
faqs.a: Yes, after choosing an authorized provider and completing a submitter agreement. The office then emails an identification number within two business days.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to record a satisfaction of a mortgage in Wayne County?
faqs.a: No. State law sets no fee for recording a satisfaction or cancellation of a deed of trust or mortgage.

faqs.q: Where do I file a will in Wayne County?
faqs.a: Wills go to the Clerk of Courts, not the Register of Deeds. The Register of Deeds page gives 919-722-6100 for the clerk's office.
